name: fig3-expression
title: Fig 3 (2G/2H) — Single-cell expression: bursty mRNA vs accumulating protein
question:
Does the reduced viva-mGen expression module (stochastic transcription +
translation + RNA/protein decay on a representative gene panel) reproduce the
qualitative single-cell gene-expression dynamics of Fig 3 / 2G-2H — bursty,
low-copy mRNA alongside protein that accumulates to much higher, more stable
copy numbers (the mRNA↔protein decoupling)?
hypothesis:
With Poisson synthesis and Poisson decay running through shared stores, mRNA
should stay low and bursty (order 0-2 copies per gene, set by short half-lives
and low synthesis rates), while protein — synthesized proportionally to mRNA
and decaying far more slowly — should accumulate to copy numbers orders of
magnitude above mRNA, reproducing the Fig 2H decoupling qualitatively.
objective:
Run the fig3_expression composite (transcription + translation + rna_decay +
protein_decay) for one hour at the default 1 s interval, gather per-gene mRNA
and protein counts, and read out mean mRNA per gene, final total protein, the
protein-to-mRNA ratio, and the fraction of panel genes expressed.
description:
REDUCED FIDELITY. This study reproduces the *qualitative* single-cell
expression phenomena of Fig 2G/2H on a representative 6-gene panel (HMW2, dnaA,
ftsZ, rpoD, tuf, groEL), NOT the full ~480-gene set. The stochastic mechanism
is genuine — Poisson mRNA synthesis, mRNA-proportional Poisson translation, and
Poisson decay of both species through shared bigraph stores — but per-species
rates are order-of-magnitude representative values, not the whole-cell model's
fitted knowledge-base rates.

DIVERGENCE (stated explicitly): this reduced panel does NOT reproduce the
paper's quantitative t50 = 18 min half-of-expression value, which is a
population statistic over the full gene set; that is out of scope here. What it
does reproduce is the decoupling itself. Achieved (seed 0, 1 h run): mean mRNA
per gene ~1.6 copies (low, bursty), final total mRNA ~9 copies across the panel
vs final total protein ~1750-2000 copies, a protein-to-mRNA ratio of ~200, and
all 6 panel genes expressed by the end. Values vary run to run — this is the
intended single-cell stochastic variability, not noise in the reproduction.

simulation_set.name: baseline
simulation_set.condition: Canonical viva-mGen fig3-expression run via sims/run.py (recorded in .pbg/runs.jsonl).

expected_behavior.name: mrna-is-bursty-low-copy
expected_behavior.en: mRNA stays low-copy and bursty — time-averaged mRNA per gene is order 0-2 copies (Fig 2G).
expected_behavior.rationale: Short mRNA half-lives (~150-180 s) and low synthesis rates keep steady-state mRNA at a fraction of one to a few copies per gene. Achieved ~1.6.

expected_behavior.name: protein-exceeds-mrna
expected_behavior.en: Protein accumulates far above mRNA — the mRNA↔protein decoupling of Fig 2H (ratio >> 1).
expected_behavior.rationale: Protein is synthesized proportionally to mRNA but decays ~150× more slowly (half-life 25000 s vs ~170 s), so it accumulates to orders of magnitude more copies than the transient mRNA pool. Achieved ~200.

expected_behavior.name: genes-become-expressed
expected_behavior.en: Every panel gene has produced protein by the end of one hour (fraction ≈ 1.0).
expected_behavior.rationale: Over an hour each gene fires enough transcription/translation events that all 6 accumulate protein. Achieved 1.000.

behavior_tests.name: mrna-is-bursty-low-copy
behavior_tests.description: Time-averaged mRNA per gene within [0, 5] copies (low, bursty).

provenance.note: Single-cell mRNA is low-copy and bursty (Karr 2012 Fig 2G); reduced panel achieved mean_mrna_per_gene ~1.6. Representative rates, not KB-fitted.

behavior_tests.name: protein-exceeds-mrna
behavior_tests.description: Final protein-to-mRNA ratio within [5, 1e9] — protein >> mRNA (decoupling).

provenance.note: mRNA and protein copy-number distributions are decoupled, protein far higher (Karr 2012 Fig 2H); achieved ratio ~200 (varies run to run).

behavior_tests.name: genes-become-expressed
behavior_tests.description: Fraction of panel genes with protein by 1 h within [0.9, 1.0].

provenance.note: Over 1 h all representative genes express; achieved 1.000.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
The expression module reproduces the qualitative Fig 2G/2H decoupling —
bursty low-copy mRNA and protein accumulating orders of magnitude higher —
on the representative gene panel. Quantitative population statistics (t50)
are explicitly out of scope for the reduced panel.

embed_visualizations.name: expression-timeseries
embed_visualizations.description: Total mRNA (bursty, low) and total protein (accumulating) across the panel over 1 h.

embed_visualizations.name: protein-vs-mrna
embed_visualizations.description: Per-gene final mRNA vs protein copy number — protein >> mRNA (Fig 2H decoupling).

conclusion:
The reduced viva-mGen expression module reproduces the qualitative single-cell
dynamics of Fig 2G/2H: mRNA stays low and bursty (mean ~1.6 copies per gene,
final total ~9 across the 6-gene panel) while protein accumulates far higher
(final total ~1750-2000 copies), a protein-to-mRNA ratio of ~200 and all 6
panel genes expressed by 1 h. Copy numbers vary run to run — the intended
single-cell stochastic variability. REDUCED FIDELITY caveat: this is a
representative 6-gene panel with order-of-magnitude rates, not the full ~480
genes with KB-fitted rates, so it deliberately does NOT reproduce the paper's
quantitative t50 = 18 min half-of-expression statistic; it establishes the
decoupling phenomenon, not that population number.
